summary.name: DataGrip
summary.one_liner: DataGrip is JetBrains' cross-platform IDE for managing relational and NoSQL databases and writing SQL, usable directly or with AI agents.
keywords: cloud database discovery aws azure google cloud
use_cases: Write and run SQL queries with schema-aware completion
Manage multiple databases from one interface
Edit query results in interactive tables
Export and import data between database formats
Let AI agents work on databases with permission controls
Review and track query history and revert changes
summary.what_it_does: DataGrip is a database IDE supporting over 50 local and cloud-based databases, including PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, Microsoft SQL, MongoDB and Redis. It offers schema-aware SQL code completion, error detection, quick-fixes and configurable formatting across multiple SQL dialects. Query results can be filtered, sorted and edited in interactive tables, visualized with no-code charts, and exported or imported in standard formats. It tracks queries run by the user or agents, provides local history for reverting changes, and integrates with Git. It can also connect to AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure accounts to discover instances, and lets AI agents (such as Junie, Claude, Codex, GitHub Copilot, or Gemini CLI) work with data sources under configurable permissions and confirmation dialogs.
notable: Free for non-commercial use, with a 30-day trial for commercial use
Agent permissions, read-only mode, and an MCP server controlling which tools agents see
Included in IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate and PyCharm Pro database tools
Cloud instance discovery on AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure
caveats: Commercial use requires a paid subscription
Free tier is limited to non-commercial use
